newsitem.title: UK: UK industry lobby group urges Blair to raise taxes.
newsitem.headline: UK industry lobby group urges Blair to raise taxes.

text.p: The head of a powerful British industry lobby group said on Monday new Prime Minister Tony Blair should prevent the country's economy from overheating by raising taxes rather than interest rates.
"Some action will probably be needed soon to slow down the economy," Confederation of British Industry (CBI) director general Adair Turner wrote in the Financial Times.
"The CBI prefers this to come via tax increases rather than through interest rate rises that could push sterling higher: those tax increases would also cut public borrowing, which is still too high."
The pound has risen almost 20 percent against the U.S. dollar since the middle of 1996 and British exporters say this is hurting them badly.

Before Labour's landslide election win last week Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown promised to announce an emergency budget within six weeks of victory. But a Labour source told the Financial Times that the budget could be put back until the end of July.
Analysts and government officials believed that a new tax rise of 10 billion pounds ($16 billion) was needed, the paper said.
